en: Sutta Nipāta 1.8 Mettasutta “By one skilled in the goal, that which is to be done must be performed:”
Having realized the state of peace,
one should be capable, upright, and very upright,
easy to speak to, gentle, and free from pride.
Contented and easy to support,
with few duties and a simple livelihood,
with senses at peace and being wise.
Free from immodesty and not greedy for the families of others,
one should not commit even the slightest act by which the wise might censure others.
May they be happy and secure;
may all beings be of a joyful mind. Whatever living creatures there are,
Whether moving or stationary,
whatever remains in the forest; whether long or large,
medium-sized, short, minute, or thick.
Those who have been seen or those not yet seen,
those who dwell far away or those who are near,
those who have come to be or those seeking birth—
May all beings be happy-minded.
Let no one deceive another,
nor despise anyone anywhere.
Free from resentment and free from ill will,
one should not wish suffering upon another,
just as a mother does not wish harm to her own child.
One should protect one's only son with one's life;
even so, one should cultivate an immeasurable mind toward all beings.
And let one cultivate a measureless mind of loving-kindness toward the entire world—
above, below, and across.
Unconfined, free from enmity, and without ill will—
whether standing, walking, sitting,
or lying down, as long as one is awake.
One should resolve upon this mindfulness;
they call this the sublime abiding here.
And without falling into views—
Virtuous and perfected in vision,
having removed greed for sensual pleasures,
one does not return to lying in a womb again at any time.
The Metta Sutta is the eighth.
